#### Is there a free Grok Bot alternative?

Yes. Three alternatives run free under open-source licenses: Hermes Agent (MIT-licensed, from Nous Research), Buzz (Apache 2.0, from Block), and OpenClaw (MIT-licensed). All three run on your own hardware with your own model provider. Viktor offers a free tier with up to $100 in credits before any charge applies. No free or freemium managed alternative does exactly what Grok Bot does (persistent bots on a cloud computer). The free options are self-hosted or credit-gated.

#### Is the Grok bot free? [...] Hermes Agent, from Nous Research, is the closest structural match to Grok Bot on this list. Persistent bots with individual model selection, persistent memory, inter-agent communication, and scheduled routines: everything Grok Bot built, running on your own hardware instead of xAI's cloud, under an MIT license and at no cost.

Hermes launched on August 18, 2026, a week after Grok Bot. It is genuinely early: beta-stage stability, no mobile version, rough edges the community is still working out. For a developer who wants the persistent-bot architecture without the subscription or the shared-credential problem, this is the first place to look. [...] Grok Bot access starts at $20 a month through Cursor Pro, but usage runs on a separate metered pool with no published cap and no audit trail shipped. Every Grok Bot alternative on this list charges a flat rate. If you want business roles handled rather than another agent to operate, Marblism gives you 7 AI Employees for $24 a month. If you want the same persistent-bot architecture running free on your own machine, Hermes Agent is the direct structural alternative. For autonomous cloud-based multi-step deliverables, Manus starts at $20 a month. For developers who want self-hosted control, Buzz and OpenClaw are both free and open-source. Most SMB owners searching for Grok Bot alternatives do not need a persistent cloud computer: they need the work done.

What is the best open source alternative to Grok Bot?

rakazo is the closest architectural match. Its bots keep their own memory and history between sessions and run on a schedule; they get browser, terminal, file, and graphical desktop access; a choice of shared or isolated compute via Docker, E2B, Daytona, or Box; and unrestricted model selection. It is Apache-2.0 licensed and fully self-hosted. Teams that need compliance controls, approval workflows, and a built-in audit trail should look at openbot instead.

Can Grok Bot be self-hosted? [...] # Best Open Source Grok Bot Alternatives

Grok Bot is xAI's agentic product, not the Grok chatbot. You set up bots once, each with its own memory and history like a teammate with a name, all working on one shared cloud computer with a browser, a filesystem and a terminal. Maybe you saw that it needs a paid Cursor or SuperGrok plan with no free tier and wondered whether a self-hosted stack can do the same work. Eight projects get close, and I ranked them by how much of that setup they keep. Some give every bot its own machine, some live in Slack or Telegram, and a couple keep an audit trail behind a policy gate. [...] The closest match to how Grok Bot works is rakazo. Its bots keep their own memory between sessions, get browser and terminal access, run on whichever model provider you plug in, and you self-host the whole Apache-2.0 stack.
